injuries.note: Left Adelaide’s NBL27 opener against Melbourne United at John Cain Arena on Saturday 19 September 2026 with an ankle injury, reported by basketball.com.au. He started the game. Michael Randall reported on 23 September that Cameron will not fly to Perth for the trip to the Wildcats. Jai at Fox Sports (@NBLPleb) reported on 27 September that Cameron is sidelined in a moon boot on his right ankle and is expected to be out for up to six weeks. That is an upper bound rather than a date, and no starting point was given for it. The NBL’s list of 20 October has his return as TBC.

Retired on October 20, 2026. Adelaide 36ers announced that a persistent knee injury had forced him to end his career, after 173 NBL games, 124 of them for Adelaide. He did not play in NBL27 and moves into a non-playing role with the club.
Expected to miss five weeks with the ankle injury from 15 October 2026, Walshly News reported on 21 October. Archie Woodhill suits up in his place.

Will miss at least six weeks with a lower leg injury, the NBL reported on 9 October 2026 in announcing that Brisbane have signed Mawot Mag as his injury replacement player. He was hurt in Brisbane’s home game against Tasmania on Saturday 3 October, the night he returned from a hand injury, and Brisbane’s update of 7 October ruled him out for about six weeks, with Josh Duach suiting up in his absence. The NBL’s list of 13 October has him back in Round 10.

Brisbane confirmed on Monday 12 October 2026 that Velicka has been ruled out with a lower limb injury and is expected to return at the start of December; the NBL’s list of 13 October has him back in Rounds 11 to 12. He was hurt in the Bullets’ game against the Cairns Taipans on Thursday 8 October. Brisbane have signed Raul Neto as his injury replacement player, the NBL announced on 13 October. Olgun Uluc of ESPN had reported on 10 October, citing sources, a quad injury of about eight weeks. Velicka was averaging 13.8 points and a league-leading 10.2 assists in NBL27.

The Taipans confirmed on 7 October 2026 that Dech will be out for at least four weeks with a hamstring injury, reported by Jai of Fox Sports (@NBLPleb). The NBL’s list of the same evening has him back in Round 8.
Illawarra announced on 9 October 2026 that he will have season-ending foot surgery, NBL.com.au reported.

Goulding missed Melbourne United’s game against Cairns at John Cain Arena on Saturday 3 October with a calf strain, according to the Taipans’ game preview of 3 October 2026. United have not given a return date; the NBL’s list of 20 October has him back in Round 7.

Melbourne United have confirmed the graft from his August 2025 reconstruction failed under rehab loading. He is having a second ACL reconstruction, 9-12 months, and is targeting a return for NBL28 pre-season.

New Zealand Breakers general manager Dillon Boucher said on 3 October 2026 that Le Gassick is managing a nerve impingement in his neck and shoulder, and that his return-to-play timeline is not yet certain, reported by Jai at Fox Sports (@NBLPleb). The NBL had listed him with an ankle injury before removing him from its list in the 26 September refresh. He has not played in NBL27.

The Breakers say James has a torn left hamstring, reported by Olgun Uluc on 16 September 2026. On 3 October general manager Dillon Boucher said James is three weeks post-injury and will be assessed at the four-to-six-week mark of his rehabilitation, reported by Jai at Fox Sports (@NBLPleb). Mojave King has joined as injury cover, and Boucher said the club will keep monitoring the import market.

Perth said on 21 October that he has had a setback with the injury and will be re-evaluated after the November FIBA break. The NBL listed his return as Round 11 on 22 October. The club had ruled him out on 1 October with a calf injury and a review in about three weeks. Development player Tana Kopa replaced him on the roster. He left Perth’s 97-93 win over the New Zealand Breakers on 26 September after 7 minutes and 38 seconds, first reported by basketball.com.au that night.

Perth have confirmed a successful reconstruction of a torn ACL in his right knee and say he is expected to miss the entirety of the 2026-27 season. He is a development player, announced by the club on 9 June 2026, and is not in our 12-man projected Perth depth chart. The NBL added him to its own list in the 21 September 2026 refresh.

The Sydney Kings said on Tuesday 13 October 2026 that Dellavedova will miss both Round 5 games, against the New Zealand Breakers on Wednesday 14 October and the Perth Wildcats on Sunday 18 October, with a calf injury, and will be re-evaluated next week. Lachlan Bofinger replaces him in the squad. The NBL’s list of 13 October has him back in Round 7.

WIN News Tasmania’s Brent Costelloe reported from the JackJumpers press conference on Wednesday 17 September that Ayre was "still a few weeks away from returning". The NBL’s list of 20 October has him back in Round 7, having listed him as a test on 13 October.

Michael Randall reported on 22 September 2026 that Deng will miss Tasmania’s trip to the Cairns Taipans on Wednesday 23 September, joining Josh Bannan, Anthony Drmic, Ben Ayre and Bryce Hamilton on the sidelines, without specifying an injury. The NBL’s own list added him as a lower leg injury in its 26 September update, and its 29 September update puts his return at Round 8-10. He did not dress against Cairns.
Tasmania have confirmed the knee injury is an ACL, and have signed Nick Stoddart as a Nominated Replacement Player to cover him for the Blitz and the start of the season.
